<document id=DOC_excerpt_settle_order>
DISCOUNT_BY_TIER = {"standard": 20, "premium": 30}

def settle_order(account_tier, total_amount, coupon_codes, coupon_lookup):
    discount = DISCOUNT_BY_TIER[account_tier]
    coupon_sum = coupon_lookup[coupon_codes[0]]
    amount_owed = total_amount * discount / 100 - coupon_sum
    return amount_owed
</document>

The module below redeems coupon codes by looking them up. Nothing in
it limits how long a code stays redeemable, so every code ever issued
remains valid indefinitely.

Recommend how the design should bound a code's lifetime, and say what
the lookup would have to carry for that bound to be enforceable.

response.text:
Bound each code with an absolute expiry instant, and make the lookup return that instant next to the value so settlement can reject the code when it is past.

**Lifetime bound.** Store an `expires_at` on every issued code (an absolute timestamp, not “valid forever unless we remember to delete it”). Optionally also store `valid_from` if codes should not redeem before a start time. Issue-time plus a TTL is fine only if you persist the computed `expires_at`; do not recompute lifetime from “now” at redeem time. Treat missing expiry as invalid, not as never-expiring.

**What the lookup must carry.** Today `coupon_lookup[code]` is a bare number (`coupon_sum`). That cannot enforce a bound. The value has to be a record that includes at least:

- the discount amount (what you subtract today)
- `expires_at` (and `valid_from` if you use a window)

Settlement must read that record, compare the redemption time to `expires_at`, and refuse the code when `now >= expires_at` (or before `valid_from`). If the lookup stays a scalar, expiry cannot be checked no matter what policy you write beside it.
